title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
content: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted input is concatenated into SQL queries. Attackers can bypass auth, read/write data, or execute commands. Prevention: parameterized queries, ORM, input validation, least privilege DB accounts, WAF.
snippet:
-- Vulnerable
query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{email}'"

-- Safe (parameterized)
query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = %s"
cursor.execute(query, (email,))

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
content: XSS injects malicious scripts into web pages viewed by others. Types: stored, reflected, DOM-based. Impact: session theft, account takeover, keylogging. Prevention: output encoding, CSP headers, sanitize input, HttpOnly cookies.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
content: CSRF tricks authenticated users into submitting unwanted requests. Attacker crafts malicious page that triggers state-changing requests. Prevention: CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, double-submit cookies, custom headers, origin checking.

title: Authentication & Session Security
content: Secure auth: bcrypt/argon2 password hashing, session rotation, JWT with short expiry, 2FA/TOTP, rate limiting, account lockout, secure cookie flags (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), password strength policies.

title: CVE-2021-44228 — Log4Shell
content: Log4Shell: critical RCE in Apache Log4j 2. Attackers send ${jndi:ldap://...} strings that trigger JNDI lookups, enabling remote code execution. Affects Java apps. Fix: upgrade to Log4j 2.17.1+, disable JNDI, block outbound LDAP.

title: CVE-2017-0144 — EternalBlue (SMB)
content: EternalBlue: critical SMBv1 vulnerability in Windows. Exploited by WannaCry ransomware. Allows remote code execution via crafted SMB packets. Fix: patch MS17-010, disable SMBv1, block port 445 at firewall.
snippet:
# Check SMBv1 status
Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol

# Disable SMBv1
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false

# Block port 445
netsh advfirewall firewall add rule dir=in action=block protocol=TCP localport=445

title: CVE-2023-44487 — HTTP/2 Rapid Reset
content: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset: DDoS amplification via rapid stream cancellation. Attackers open many streams then immediately reset them, exhausting server resources. Fix: apply vendor patches, rate limit streams, upgrade HTTP/2 implementations.
snippet:
# Mitigation strategies
- Apply vendor patches (nginx, Apache, Node.js)
- Limit concurrent streams per connection
- Monitor RST_STREAM rates
- Use DDoS protection services

title: CVE-2021-34527 — PrintNightmare
content: PrintNightmare: RCE in Windows Print Spooler. Allows remote code execution with SYSTEM privileges via crafted print jobs. Fix: apply patches, disable Print Spooler if unused, restrict Point and Print.
snippet:
# Disable Print Spooler (if not needed)
Stop-Service Spooler
Set-Service Spooler -StartupType Disabled

# Registry hardening
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint
NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall = 0

title: CVE-2021-26855 — ProxyLogon (Exchange)
content: ProxyLogon: SSRF in Microsoft Exchange Server allowing unauthenticated RCE. Chain with CVE-2021-27065 for webshell deployment. Fix: apply March 2021 patches, check for webshells, audit logs.
snippet:
# Check for webshells
Get-ChildItem -Path C:\inetpub\wwwroot -Recurse -Filter *.aspx

# Check for suspicious files
Get-ChildItem -Path C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client -Recurse

title: Encryption & Hashing Explained
content: Encryption is reversible (AES, RSA). Hashing is one-way (SHA-256, bcrypt). Symmetric uses one key (AES-256-GCM). Asymmetric uses key pairs (RSA, ECC). Use AES-256-GCM for data at rest, TLS 1.3 for transit, bcrypt/argon2 for passwords.
snippet:
# AES-256-GCM (Python)
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
key = AESGCM.generate_key(bit_length=256)
aesgcm = AESGCM(key)
ct = aesgcm.encrypt(nonce, b'data', None)

# Password hashing
bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt(12))

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
content: SSRF: attacker makes server fetch arbitrary URLs, accessing internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), or localhost. Prevention: allowlist domains, block private IPs, validate redirects, disable unnecessary protocols.
snippet:
# Block private IPs
import ipaddress
ip = ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)
if ip.is_private or ip.is_loopback or ip.is_link_local:
    raise ValueError('Blocked')

# Cloud metadata
169.254.169.254  # AWS/GCP/Azure metadata

title: API Security Best Practices
content: API security: authentication (OAuth2/JWT), authorization (RBAC), rate limiting, input validation, HTTPS/TLS, CORS restrictions, API keys rotation, audit logging, error handling without info leak, versioning.
snippet:
// Security headers
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: DENY

// Rate limit
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 99

title: Zero Trust Security Model
content: Zero Trust: never trust, always verify. Principles: verify explicitly, least privilege access, assume breach. Components: MFA, device compliance, micro-segmentation, continuous monitoring, identity-based access.
snippet:
Zero Trust Pillars:
1. Identity - MFA, SSO
2. Device - compliance checks
3. Network - micro-segmentation
4. Data - encryption, DLP
5. Workload - secure containers
6. Visibility - continuous monitoring

title: Password Security & NIST Guidelines
content: NIST guidelines: use passphrases (15+ chars), check against breach lists, allow paste in password fields, no forced periodic rotation, support all characters, rate-limit attempts, use password managers.
snippet:
Strong passphrase example:
correct-horse-battery-staple

NIST SP 800-63B:
- Length > 15 chars
- Check against breached passwords
- No composition rules (no forced symbols)
- No periodic rotation
- Allow paste
- Rate limit login attempts

title: TLS/HTTPS Explained
content: TLS encrypts data in transit. TLS 1.3 is current standard. Certificates verify identity via CA chain. HSTS forces HTTPS. Key exchange: ECDHE. Cipher suites: AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20. Disable TLS 1.0/1.1.

title: CVE-2014-0160 — Heartbleed
content: Heartbleed: buffer over-read in OpenSSL heartbeat extension. Allows reading server memory including private keys, passwords, session tokens. Affects OpenSSL 1.0.1-1.0.1f. Fix: upgrade OpenSSL, revoke/reissue certificates, rotate secrets.
snippet:
# Detection
openssl s_client -connect host:443 -tlsextdebug 2>&1 | grep 'server extension'

# Fix
- Upgrade to OpenSSL 1.0.1g+
- Reissue all certificates
- Rotate all passwords/keys
- Invalidate sessions

title: CVE-2019-19781 — Citrix ADC
content: CVE-2019-19781: directory traversal in Citrix ADC/NetScaler allowing unauthenticated RCE. Exploited for webshells and ransomware. Fix: apply vendor patches, check for webshells, restrict management access.
snippet:
# Check for webshells
find /var/tmp -name '*.pl' -o -name '*.xml'

# Mitigation
- Apply Citrix patches
- Block external access to management UI
- Check /netscaler/portal/templates/

title: CVE-2020-1472 — Zerologon
content: Zerologon: privilege escalation in Netlogon (MS-NRPC). Attacker can impersonate domain controller and take over Active Directory. Fix: apply August 2020 patches, enforce secure RPC, monitor Event ID 5827/5828.
snippet:
# Check for vulnerable DCs
Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair

# Monitor
Event ID 5827: Netlogon secure channel denied
Event ID 5828: Netlogon secure channel allowed

# Fix: Apply KB4565349+

title: CVE-2023-23397 — Outlook NTLM
content: CVE-2023-23397: Outlook vulnerability allowing NTLM credential theft via crafted calendar invites. Attacker sends meeting with UNC path triggering NTLM hash leak. Fix: apply March 2023 patches, block TCP 445 outbound, add firewall rules.
snippet:
# Mitigation
- Apply March 2023 Outlook patches
- Block outbound SMB (TCP 445)
- Add users to Protected Users group
- Enable Extended Protection for Authentication
